title: Raynaud schematicity for separated locally finite-type group spaces over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and set $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], equipped with morphisms $m:X\times_S X\to X$, $e:S\to X$, and $i:X\to X$ satisfying the group identities; commutativity is not required. Suppose $X\to S$ is separated, meaning that its representable diagonal is a closed immersion on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion], and locally of finite type, meaning locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $X$ is represented by an $S$-scheme. No quasi-compactness, smoothness, finite-type generic fibre, or affine-neighbourhood hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Raynaud, Specialisation du foncteur de Picard, Publications Mathematiques IHES 38 (1970), Theoreme 3.3.1, printed p.40 (PDF p.15); specialization of the locally Noetherian normal dimension-one base to a DVR. This theorem says locally of finite type, not finite type. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read at https://numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1970__38__27_0.pdf.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ and let $k=R/(\pi)$. The fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with group laws obtained by pulling back those of $X$. It is separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Pull back an etale scheme atlas of $X$ to obtain an atlas of $X_s$; its charts remain locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Thus $X_s/k$ is a locally finite-type, locally separated group space (a closed-immersion diagonal is in particular an immersion). Apply [lem-sfb-locally-separated-group-space-scheme] to conclude that $X_s$ is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0B8F (lemma-group-space-scheme-locally-finite-type-over-k); Anantharaman 4.1, printed p.55, special fibres

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ put $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(\pi^n))$ and $X_n=X\times_SS_n$. These are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The closed immersion $X_s\hookrightarrow X_n$ is a thickening: on scheme tests its ideal is generated by the image of $\pi$, whose $n$-th power is zero, so every prime contains that ideal. It induces a homeomorphism on point spaces because this is true on the etale scheme charts. Since its source is the scheme of step 1, [lem-sfb-thickening-of-scheme-space] makes every $X_n$ a scheme. This uses neither reducedness nor flatness of $X$.

source.place: Tag 05ZR (lemma-thickening-scheme); Anantharaman 4.1, printed p.55, infinitesimal fibre neighbourhoods

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-trait-flat-group-closure] to $X$. Its hypotheses are the given separatedness and local finite type, with no flatness hypothesis. Obtain a closed group subspace $C\hookrightarrow X$ whose ideal on an etale affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ is $\ker(B\to B[1/\pi])$. It is the full generic-fibre closure, has $C_K=X_K$, and is separated, flat and locally of finite type over $S$. In particular the group structure needed below exists on this closure.

Apply [lem-sfb-flat-group-space-fpqc-scheme-cover] to the flat group space $C$. This supplies an fpqc morphism $T\to S$ and a separated flat $T$-group scheme $P$ locally of finite presentation representing $C_T$ as a group sheaf. The lemma supplies local finite presentation even when $T$ is not Noetherian; no finiteness assertion about the total space $C$ or $P$ is used.

By [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf], the algebraic space $C$ satisfies the fpqc sheaf equalizer condition on scheme tests. Its restricted group operations make it an fpqc sheaf of groups. With $F=C$, apply [lem-sfb-trait-flat-group-fpqc-effectivity] to the cover and group scheme of step 4: the base is the original trait, and the representing scheme over $T$ is separated, flat and locally of finite presentation. Hence $C$ is represented by a scheme.

source.place: Theorem 4.A, flat case, and 4.2 Step 3 (4.A implies 4.B), printed pp.53 and 56; fpqc-sheaf hypothesis supplied by Stacks Tag 04P2 (and Tag 0APL), not by the fppf definition alone

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-trait-space-closure-thickenings-scheme] with $Y=X$, its horizontal closure $C$ from step 3, and the spaces $X_n$ from step 2. The kernel formula in step 3 is exactly its required schematic closure; step 5 represents $C$, and step 2 represents every $X_n$. The given $X/S$ is separated and locally of finite type, so all its hypotheses hold. It follows that $X$ is represented by an $S$-scheme, as asserted.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.2, printed pp.20-21; 4.2 Step 2, printed p.56

lean.statement: theorem exists_scheme_of_trait_group {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of R))) (F : (Over (Spec (.of R)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{u}) (e : F ⋙ forget GrpCat ≅ X.obj.obj) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 X.obj.obj) (𝟙 X.obj.obj))) (hlft : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of R))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale a → LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) : ∃ Y : Over (Spec (.of R)), Nonempty (X.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj Y)
lean.note: The given noncommutative group operations are encoded by a GrpCat-valued functor F with an identification e of its underlying presheaf with X, as in the recorded field-case theorem. Separatedness is scheme-test closed representability of the diagonal; local finite type is tested on all representable etale scheme charts. The conclusion represents the same space by a scheme over Spec R, without quasi-compactness or flatness assumptions.
